entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: Surepalli Nanda
Bench: Surepalli Nanda
 Hon'Ble Mrs Justice Surepalli Nanda
 Writ Petition No.31814 Of 2023
Order:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.P.Pallavi, learned counsel representing learned Deputy Solicitor General of India appearing for respondents.

2. This writ petition is filed to issue an appropriate writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of Mandamus declaring the inaction of the respondent No.1 in reissuing the passport of petitioner bearing No.W0578547 pursuant to his passport application with file No.HY2075579666123, dated 17.07.2023, as illegal, arbitrary and violation of principles of natural justice and against law and consequently, direct the respondent No.1 to reissue the passport of petitioner bearing passport No.W0578547 by considering his passport application with file No.
No.HY2075579666123, dated 17.07.2023 without reference to the pendency of the Criminal Cases.
3.

The case of the petitioner, in brief, is as under:
a) The petitioner herein is holder of passport bearing No.W0578547 and it is valid upto 01.05.2032.
However, the petitioner lost the passport and had applied for reissuance of passport through online vide application No.HY2075579666123 dated 17.07.2023.

The same was not considered by the SN, J respondent No.1 on the ground that the petitioner is accused in criminal cases and the respondent No.1 has sought clarifications from the petitioner through letter dated 24.08.2023.

Therefore,
the petitioner submitted an explanation vide letter dated 18.09.2023 and also met them personally and requested for reissuance of the passport.
Even then, respondent No.1 is not considering the request made by the petitioner seeking reissue of the passport.
Therefore, the present Writ Petition.

b) Petitioner herein is an accused in C.C.No.4852 of 2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 420, 406, 468, 471 and read with 34 of IPC and it is pending for final disposal and the petitioner herein is also an accused in another C.C.No.4955 of 2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 468, 471, 34, 120B of IPC and it is pending for final disposal.

It is the specific plea of the petitioner that the respondent cannot refuse the reissue of passport of the petitioner on the ground of the pendency of the aforesaid criminal cases against the petitioner and the said action of the respondent is contrary to the procedure laid down under the Passports Act,
M. Naval Kishore Reddy vs Regional Passport Office on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152807615/
1 1967 and also the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu v. Central Bureau of Investigation 1.

sentences.text: Hence, this writ petition.

. 2020 Crl.L.J. (SC)
572 SN, J PERUSED THE RECORD 4.

It is relevant to note that the Apex Court in Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu (supra) had an occasion to examine the provisions of the Passports Act, 1967, pendency of criminal cases and held that refusal of a passport can be only in case where an applicant is convicted during the period of five (05) years immediately preceding the date of application for an offence involving moral turpitude and sentence for imprisonment for not less than two years.
Section 6.2(f) relates to a situation where the applicant is facing trial in a criminal Court.

The petitioner therein was convicted in a case for the offences under Sections 420 IPC and also Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, against which, an appeal was filed and the same was dismissed.
The sentence was reduced to a period of one (01) year.
The petitioner therein had approached the Apex Court by way of filing an appeal and the same is pending.

Therefore,
considering the said facts, the Apex Court held that Passport Authority cannot refuse renewal of the passport on the ground of pendency of the criminal appeal.
Thus, the Apex Court directed the Passport Authority to renew the passport of the applicant without raising the objection relating to the pendency of the aforesaid criminal appeal in S.C. SN, J 5.

It is represented by learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel appearing for the respondents that the subject issue in the present writ petition is squarely covered by the order of this Court dated 06.10.2023 passed in W.P.No.27831 of 2023.
6.

sentences.text:
The Respondent-Passport Officer shall consider the said application in the light of the observations made by this Court herein as well as the contents of the undertaking given by the petitioner for reissue of his passport in accordance with law, within two (03) weeks from the date of said application;
v) On reissue of the Passport, the petitioner herein shall deposit the original reissue Passport before the trial Court in C.C.Nos.4852 and 4955 of 2022; and vi) However, liberty is granted to the petitioner herein to file an application before the trial Court seeking permission to travel aboard and it is for the trial Court to consider the same in accordance with law.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petition shall also stand closed.
However, in the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.

___ MRS JUSTICE SUREPALLI NANDA Date: 17.11.2023 kgk M. Naval Kishore Reddy vs Regional Passport Office on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152807615/
